Historical findings CASEID FILE NOTE
1) Domain context: A generic institutional records office files ordinary paperwork as discrete records: each intake generates a document ID, a date field, a holder field, and a channel field. Files are cross-indexed by account and date. Access is logged per account per date. No narrative content is stored; only structured fields are indexed and retained.

2) What occurred: The actor opened a records request (a document) on a dated date, citing a single ticket record. The actor filed a request to replicate the ticket record, generating multiple derived documents sharing the same source document ID. The actor filed a channel record indicating a transfer of possession of the replicated documents to a second account. The actor filed a note field specifying that the second account should present the replicated documents at the gate before the first account. The actor filed a hold field requesting that no refund record, no chargeback record, and no identity-verification record be opened against either account for the transaction date.

3) Materials/access observed: A valid ticket record (single, named account, dated). Replicated ticket records (multiple, same source document ID, derived field marked). A transfer document between two named accounts. A channel record (presentation at gate, dated). A hold document covering three fields: refund, chargeback, identity verification. Access was logged under the first account's name for all derived documents.

4) Indicators & artifacts: Multiple derived documents with identical source document ID on a single date. A transfer document referencing gate presentation by the receiving account before the holding account. A hold document requesting suppression of three standard record types (refund, chargeback, identity verification) for a specific date and account pair. All artifacts linked by a single account identifier and a single date field.
